canal.name: River Navigation Canal
canal.description: Weirs with flash locks, dredged channels and towpaths carry boats past the shallows next to this location. The waterway stays open while any bank keeps such a canal.

navigable.name: Navigable River
navigable.description: A river reach that boats can use.

improvable.name: Shallows
improvable.description: Shoals and mill weirs: boats pass slowly and at a cost until a River Navigation Canal is built on a bank.

barrier.name: Falls
barrier.description: Falls and great rapids that boats cannot pass.

starting_evidence.note: Maintained grain-navigation channels of the Grand Canal: shallows in this envelope start with a canal.
Basin channels kept open; the cataracts stay Falls.
Water-board authority documented from 1289. No industrial canals or steam drainage.

notes: Channel tiles take the topography of their World Builder state: navigable -> Navigable River, improvable -> Shallows, barrier -> Falls (impassable through the impassable_mountains list).

One building, the River Navigation Canal, on any bank of a Shallows tile that is not open yet (1 level). A Shallows tile is open while any bank next to it has the canal; its water roads switch between their own cost profile and 'improved' (recomputed on build and destruction, never toggled).
Shallows in a starting_evidence envelope start with a canal on their best bank.

Physical conversion thresholds and each route cost profile come from the World Builder handover; road_costs here override what each profile costs in game (step = MARKET_SEA_DISTANCE_FACTOR x (1 + market_access)).
